questions.question: A card on the classroom word wall has 4 straight sides. Both pairs of opposite sides are parallel, all 4 corners are right angles (90°), and the card measures 8 cm long and 3 cm wide. Which name fits this shape best?
questions.explain: Two pairs of parallel sides plus four 90° corners makes it a rectangle. The common trap is calling every right-angled quadrilateral a square — a square also needs all 4 sides equal, and here 8 cm is not 3 cm.

questions.question: Which statement is true about every pyramid?
options: It has one base, and all of its other faces are triangles that meet at one point called the apex.
It has two identical parallel bases joined by rectangles.
Its base must always be a triangle.
All of its faces are exactly the same shape and size.
questions.explain: A pyramid has one base and one apex where all the triangular faces meet; two identical parallel bases means it is a prism instead. The usual mix-up is thinking a pyramid must have a triangle base — the base can be any polygon.

questions.question: Sofia is wrapping a gift in a box shaped like a cube. How many edges does a cube have?
questions.explain: Count in groups: 4 edges around the top, 4 around the bottom, and 4 upright edges joining them, so 12 in all. The trap is answering 6 (that is the number of faces) or 8 (that is the number of vertices).

questions.question: At the Granville Island market, a chocolate box has two identical parallel faces that are hexagons, joined by 6 rectangular side faces. What is the correct name for this solid?
questions.explain: Name a solid by its base shape first, then say prism or pyramid: hexagon bases plus rectangles between them gives a hexagonal prism. The common mistake is naming it from the rectangular side faces instead of from the base.

questions.question: A tile on a Kelowna bathroom floor has 4 sides that are each 5 cm long, and its opposite sides are parallel. Its corners are two 60° angles and two 120° angles. Which name always fits this tile?
options: Trapezoid, because it has exactly one pair of parallel sides
questions.explain: Four equal sides with both pairs of opposite sides parallel makes a rhombus; a square or rectangle would also need 90° corners, which this tile does not have. The trap is jumping from all sides equal straight to square without checking the angles.

questions.question: Liam cuts along the edges of an empty cereal box and flattens it into a net made of 6 rectangles. When he tapes it back into the box, how many edges and how many vertices does the box have?
questions.explain: A rectangular prism has 4 top edges, 4 bottom edges and 4 upright edges (12), and one corner point at each of the 4 top and 4 bottom corners (8 vertices). The trap is swapping the two numbers — edges are the folds, vertices are the corner points.

questions.question: A paper lantern at the Richmond Night Market has 5 faces, 8 edges and 5 vertices. The face it rests on is a square. What is the correct name for this solid?
questions.explain: Take away the square base and 4 faces are left, and with only 5 vertices they must be triangles meeting at 1 apex above the 4 base corners, so it is a pyramid named by its square base. The trap is naming it from the triangular side faces instead of the base.

questions.question: Ethan's chocolate bar box has 2 identical parallel triangular faces at the ends and 3 rectangular faces in between. He says it must be a triangular pyramid because it has triangles on it. Which response is correct?
options: He is right — any solid with triangular faces is a pyramid.
It is a pyramid, and the two triangles are its two bases.
It is a prism, but it should be called a rectangular prism because 3 of its faces are rectangles.
It is a prism: the 2 identical parallel triangles are its bases, while a pyramid has only 1 base with all other faces meeting at a single apex.
questions.explain: Decide prism or pyramid by the bases: two identical parallel bases means prism, one base plus an apex means pyramid, so this is a triangular prism. The two traps here are letting triangular faces signal pyramid, and naming the solid from its side faces rather than its bases.
